faq: What technology do you build with?

We pick common, well supported tools such as a React or Next.js front end and a hosted Postgres database, unless you have a preference. We explain the choice in plain words so another developer can take over.
Who owns the code and hosting?
You do. We create the code repository and hosting in accounts you own, and add us as collaborators. When the work is done, the code and access stay with you.
What if my idea needs more than five workflows?
Then version one is too big. Order Product Scoping first so we agree what to cut. Anything beyond the package can be quoted as a separate fixed price piece of work.
Is the product secure and ready for many users?
We follow standard practice for passwords, access and data handling. An MVP is built to learn quickly, not to carry heavy traffic. We tell you what to strengthen if usage grows.

desc:
SaaS MVP development turns your idea into a first version that real people can sign up for and use. Ecom Swift LLC builds your chosen core workflows with login, a database and a clean interface, then puts the product online in your own hosting account.

## What is a SaaS MVP build?

An MVP, or minimum viable product, is the smallest working version of your software that solves one real problem for real users. It is not a demo and it is not the full vision. It has a sign-up, a database that remembers things and the few workflows that prove whether people want the product.

A first version build means someone writes that software, connects it to hosting and hands it over, so you can put it in front of customers instead of describing it to them.

## Why building small beats building big

The most common way early products fail is by taking too long to learn anything. A founder spends months on settings pages, themes and edge cases, then discovers that users wanted something different. Every feature you build before talking to users is a guess, and guesses are expensive.

A tight first version lets you test the guess cheaply. If people sign up and come back, you know where to invest. If they do not, you have lost far less time and can change direction while the code is still small.

## How a first version affects your business

A live product changes the conversations you can have. Prospects react to something they can click, not a slide. Early users report what is missing in their own words, and those words become your roadmap. Investors, partners and potential co-founders take a working product more seriously than a document.

The scope you choose shapes the result. Picking one to five workflows forces a clear answer to what the product is for. That clarity helps marketing, pricing and onboarding later, because there is a single story to tell.

## What a good first version includes

- A clear core workflow that works from the first click to the finished result.
- Email sign-up and login, with a password reset that works.
- A real database, so data persists between visits.
- A responsive layout that works on phones and laptops.
- Transactional emails such as welcome and password messages.
- A basic admin view so you can see who has signed up.
- Hosting in your own account, with a custom address when ready.
- Separate staging and live environments for safe changes.
- Payments connected for one plan when you are ready to charge.
- Source code and a handover guide that any developer can follow.

## How we build it

We begin by agreeing the workflows, in plain language, and the pages each one needs. We then build the data model, the screens and the logic, test them as a new user would and deploy to hosting that you own. You see working progress rather than a long silence.

The Basic package delivers one core workflow, a few pages, login and hosting. Standard widens that to several workflows, more pages, transactional emails, a simple admin view and a layout that adapts to phones. Premium goes further, with more workflows and pages, one payment plan, staging and live environments and a walkthrough call. Extra work beyond the chosen scope is handled as an add-on, not a surprise.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Choose the one problem your product must solve and describe it in a sentence.
- Cut every feature that is not needed for the first real user.
- Show the product to a handful of people as soon as it works.
- Keep hosting and code in accounts you own.
- Write down what you learn from early users.

**Avoid:**
- Adding settings, roles and dashboards before anyone uses the core feature.
- Waiting for perfection before showing anyone.
- Changing the scope every few days.
- Copying a large competitor feature for feature.
- Treating the first version as the final design.

## Who this service is for

Non-technical founders with a validated idea and no development team are the clearest fit. Domain experts, such as a consultant or clinic owner, who want to turn a manual process into software also benefit. Teams that finished a clickable prototype and now need real code can use this as the next step.

## What we need from you

A short description of the problem and your target user, a list of the workflows in priority order, and any designs or examples you like. We ask you to create the hosting and database accounts so you own them, and we work as a developer or collaborator. We never need your passwords.
